name: Bengaluru flyover case studies
type: case studies and validation datasets (consultancy microsimulation reports, peer review, before/after evidence) for Bengaluru flyovers and junctions
maintainer: IIT-B Hebbal report: Prof. Archak Mittal, IIT Bombay, consultancy for client Rithwik Projects Pvt Ltd (its role in the project is not stated in the report), dated 10 Aug 2026, published by OpenCity under the BBMP Hebbal tunnel dataset. Review: Prof. Ashish Verma, IST Lab, IISc Bengaluru (Sept 2026). RITES Ltd for BMRCL/GoK: Hebbal capacity augmentation and MMI hub study (15 Dec 2021). Silk Board double-decker: built by BMRCL; before/after figures from Bengaluru Traffic Police via press.
first_release: RITES Hebbal study: LOA 8 Mar 2019, interim Aug 2019, final feasibility Apr 2020, revised Jan 2021, public extract 15 Dec 2021. Silk Board double-decker first opened 17-18 July 2024. IIT-B report 10 Aug 2026.
last_activity: IIT-B report and IISc review uploaded to OpenCity 2026-09-30; finance department comments 2026-10-11; press coverage of the Silk Board/Ragigudda downstream jam on 2026-05-04 after the full double-decker opening.
licence: OpenCity lists the Hebbal tunnel dataset and the RITES Hebbal dataset as 'Other (Public Domain)' (Government of Karnataka / BMRCL documents). The IIT-B report carries a consultancy disclaimer (technical opinion of the faculty member, not IIT Bombay). Press articles are copyrighted.
code_availability: Reports only (PDF). No model files, network files or VISSIM .inpx are published for any Bengaluru case.
maintenance_health: N/A (static reports). The Hebbal debate is live: tunnel work underway since June 2026, expected completion end of Jan 2028, and the IIT-B study is publicly contested.
mixed_traffic_support: IIT-B Hebbal: says the model should distinguish at least two-wheelers, cars, auto-rickshaws, LCVs, buses and heavy vehicles, with IRC PCU factors; no composition table is reported. RITES Hebbal 2051 input (veh/h): car 8,354, taxi 6,266, two-wheeler 11,835 (35% of vehicles), auto 2,437, private/KSRTC bus 1,044, LCV 1,392, truck 1,741, multi-axle 696; total 33,765 veh = 41,596 PCU, plus 728-1,197 BMTC buses per hour depending on scenario.
non_lane_behaviour: None of the Bengaluru studies reports modelling non-lane movement; both Hebbal studies used VISSIM-style lane-based links and connectors (the IIT-B report's calibration table names 'vehicle inputs', 'connectors', 'desired speed distributions'; the RITES slides are titled 'TRAFFIC SIMULATION (VISSIM)'). The IISc review notes flyover pier footprints reducing at-grade capacity were not modelled.
seepage_filtering_support: Not addressed in any of the studies found.
per_class_parameters: Only PCU factors are recoverable. RITES implied PCU/veh: car, taxi, auto 1.0; two-wheeler 0.75; bus 3.0; LCV 2.0; truck 4.0; multi-axle 4.0. Hebbal DPR design values: elevated lane width 3.5 m, at-grade lane width 3.0 m, design speed 80/60 km/h, ramps 30 km/h, Mekhri rotary 30-40 km/h. Critics (S. Arikutharam, ex-DULT) say the 1990s PCU factors may overstate the two-wheeler contribution by about 30%.
indian_calibration_evidence: (1) IIT-B Hebbal (software not named in the report; the aerial backdrop is Microsoft/Bing imagery and the terminology matches PTV Vissim [uncertain]): network = Mekhri Circle - Bellary Road/NH-44 - CBI Junction - Veterinary College - Hebbal interchange plus ORR feeders, about 1.8-2.2 km of project corridor; morning peak 09:00-10:00; observed 32,770 veh/h (31,758 PCU) at Hebbal and 28,493 veh/h (27,863 PCU) at Mekhri Circle; observed speeds Anand Nagar->Hebbal 2.0 km in about 28 min (4.29 km/h), Esteem Mall->Hebbal down-ramp/Baptist Hospital 1.36 km in about 38 min (3.57 km/h), Sanjay Nagar Main Road 3.0 km in about 22 min (8.3 km/h); DPR V/C 2.65 (Yelahanka->City, 6,351 PCU/h) and 2.14 (City->Airport, 7,699 PCU/h). Scenarios actually reported: Base vs combined elevated corridor (1.78 km, 4-lane, 4 ramps) + 2.228 km 3-lane tunnel, at 50% and 80% assumed diversion. Results: base 13.74 km/h, 3,573.5 veh-h delay, 24,878 completed trips, 39.07 stops/trip, 517 s delay/trip; combined at 50%: 20.64 km/h (+50%), 2,480.1 veh-h (-31%), 28,865 trips (+16%), 21.3 stops, 309 s; at 80%: 22.0 km/h (+60%), 2,276.8 veh-h (-36%), 29,068 trips (+17%), 18.7 stops, 282 s. Conclusion text also cites a flyover-only run (2,209.9 veh-h, 296 s/trip) not tabulated. 2047: base 12.18 km/h, 10.20 min delay/trip; combined 16.82 km/h / 7.09 min (50%) and 15.56 km/h / 7.96 min (80%). (2) RITES Hebbal VISSIM 2019 base: 14 directional link volumes, GEH < 10 for 85% (e.g. Hebbal->Airport 6,969 obs vs 6,125 sim, GEH 9.43; Nagavara flyover EB 7,396 vs 6,265, GEH 13.68; Mekhri flyover SB 4,693 vs 3,910, GEH 11.94); section speeds observed 16-29 km/h vs simulated 18-25 km/h; 2051 Proposal-4 scenario speeds 38-44 km/h and section travel times cut from 132-220 s to 58-105 s. (3) Silk Board double-decker (BTP data via Deccan Herald, measured about two months after the 18 July 2024 opening): 56% reduction in junction congestion, morning peak -42%, evening peak -45%; queue at Ragigudda jumped to about 6 km/day in the first week then eased to about 1 km [uncertain: press-reported, original BTP data not published]. (4) VISSIM signal-optimisation papers on ORR (Silk Board and Iblur; Sarakki junction) exist in i-manager journals [uncertain: results not read].
calibration_dataset_used: IIT-B: DPR data only - 24-hour classified videographic counts on a typical working day, peak-hour turning counts, Hebbal ramp observations, speed-delay runs; no OD survey; signal timings not recorded ('represented on an assumed basis'); no pedestrian/NMT counts. RITES: July 2019 daily and peak-hour turning counts at Hebbal (398,875 PCU/day; 26,896 PCU peak hour) and link volumes on the Nagavara, Bhadrappa and Mekhri flyovers. Neither dataset is released in machine-readable form; both are in public-domain PDFs on OpenCity.
calibration_method: IIT-B: manual calibration matrix - volumes (vehicle inputs, OD matrix, turning proportions) vs junction/link counts; travel time and speed vs speed-delay survey (desired speed, car-following, signal control, route choice); queue length vs videos (saturation, lane change, signal timing); ramp interaction vs Hebbal observations (merge priority, connector placement). No error metric (GEH/RMSE) is reported; same demand and random seeds across scenarios, 30+ replications recommended but count used not stated. RITES: GEH statistic on 14 link volumes (target GEH < 10 for 85% of links met) plus comparison of 6 section speeds.
max_density_tested: Not reported in any study; IIT-B lists density (veh/km/lane) as a metric but publishes no values.
validation_against_field_case: Hebbal is the strongest candidate validation case: an open RITES 2019 GEH table and section speeds, an open IIT-B base-case summary (13.74 km/h, 3,573.5 veh-h) and its documented conflict with observed DPR speeds (4.29 and 3.57 km/h), plus a BTP fixed-time plan for the at-grade Ring Road x Bellary Road junction under the flyover (4 phases incl. pedestrian, cycle 130 s off-peak / 160 s peak). Silk Board is a qualitative scenario template (flyover relieves the junction, queue moves to the Ragigudda exit) with only percentage figures.
network_import: Studies coded their networks by hand on aerial imagery; nothing reusable. For our build the same corridors are well represented in OSM: Hebbal flyover ways (e.g. way 377852248, trunk lanes=3 layer=1; ramp way 379862163 lanes=2 layer=2), Silk Board flyover and double-decker ways with layer 1/2, Tin Factory flyover (2 x 241 m, lanes=2, layer=1).
demand_input_formats: Reports give PCU turning diagrams per approach (RITES), junction totals and classified mode volumes; IIT-B splits demand into strategic OD groups (Airport/Yelahanka<->City, Yeshwanthpur<->Hebbal, KR Puram/ORR<->Hebbal, local Sanjay Nagar/CBI) and imposes route diversion of 50-80% because no OD survey exists.
data_access: OpenCity CKAN dataset 6b11c60b-2d6d-4426-acfa-1e5464759137 (Hebbal tunnel: DPR Sept 2025, drawings, EPC agreement, RFP, IIT-B report, IISc review, finance department comments) - direct PDF downloads, no registration. RITES Hebbal report: OpenCity dataset 'capacity-augmentation-of-road-and-rail-infrastructure-at-hebbal-junction', 33-page PDF. BTP signal plans: OpenCity 'bengaluru-city-traffic-signal-data' (Hebbal Fly Over & Kodigehalli Gate; Sarjapur Road Checkpost & Silk Board; HSR 14th Main & Iblur; Bhashyam Circle & Mekhri Circle; Palmgrove & Richmond Circle; Mariappa Circle & Nagavara). Silk Board figures only in press articles.
reuse_mode: Use as data and as scenario templates. Recommended demo corridor: Hebbal, city-bound along Bellary Road/NH-44 - the Hebbal flyover (trunk mainline, 3 lanes per direction, layer 1, with layer-2 ramp), the signalised at-grade Ring Road x Bellary Road junction beneath it (BTP 4-phase plan), and the next downstream point where city-bound traffic lands near Baptist Hospital/Veterinary College towards CBI Junction (the IIT-B 'Esteem Mall -> Hebbal down-ramp/Baptist Hospital' 1.36 km run at 3.57 km/h) [uncertain: exact name and signal status of the first downstream junction must be confirmed on OSM]. Reasons: (a) only Bengaluru site with open numeric calibration targets (RITES GEH table, 26,896 PCU peak-hour turning diagram, section speeds) and a published base-case result to compare against; (b) a real BTP signal plan exists for the junction under the flyover; (c) OSM flyover and ramp ways already carry lanes and layer (including a layer-2 ramp), so the z-level pipeline is exercised; (d) it carries three ready-made scenario templates: add an elevated corridor/tunnel (IIT-B), widen flyover to 5 lanes per direction (RITES Proposal-4), and incident/lane-blockage at the flyover merge (IIT-B section 9.4, never run); (e) the public controversy (congestion shifting, diversion assumptions, PCU factors) is exactly what an interactive what-if tool can demonstrate. Silk Board double-decker -> Ragigudda is the backup template for 'flyover moves the queue downstream' but its geometry (ramps A-E, metro deck, 3.3 km) is bigger and has no published counts.
effort_within_72_hours: About 6-8 hours of data work: clip the Hebbal box from Overpass (about 13.025-13.045 N, 77.585-77.600 E), keep the NH-44 mainline, one ramp pair and the at-grade junction (drop the ORR loops and the service-road web), transcribe the BTP 4-phase plan and the RITES 2019 peak-hour turning PCUs for the four approaches, convert PCU to vehicles with the RITES mode split, and hard-code the 14 RITES directional volumes as validation checkpoints. Cut: the full four-loop cloverleaf, Mekhri Circle rotary, tunnel scenario, route choice (use fixed turning ratios), evening peak, 2047 forecasts.
licence_constraint: Government reports are public domain on OpenCity, so quoting their counts and timings in the app is fine; cite them. The IIT-B report's disclaimer means its numbers should be presented as one consultant's model output, not observed truth. Press numbers should be cited, not redistributed in bulk.
known_limitations: IIT-B report (per the report itself and the IISc review): only 2 of 4 promised scenarios reported (flyover-only and tunnel-only results not tabulated); diversion fixed at 50%/80% from the tunnel DPR and also applied to the 2+2-lane elevated corridor; no OD survey, no recorded signal timings, no pedestrian counts; software, parameters and replications not documented; queue length, density, V/C and LOS promised but not reported; incident scenarios listed but not simulated; induced demand, mode shift and pier footprint ignored; network-level analysis effectively limited to the Mekhri-Hebbal link; base speed 13.74 km/h vs observed 4.29 km/h; data predates the January 2026 Hebbal ramp opening; a figure appears to mislabel Hebbal as Mekhri Circle. RITES: GEH > 10 on 2 of 14 links (Nagavara EB 13.68, Mekhri SB 11.94); 2051 runs assume a large public-transport shift (PT scenario 2: 65:35). Silk Board: only press-reported percentages, no counts or travel times.
documented_failures: (1) Silk Board double-decker: junction congestion fell (BTP: -56%), but the queue moved to the Ragigudda exit - about 6 km/day in the first week after opening, and in May 2026 vehicles descending at Ragigudda met a signal and a queue backing onto the flyover; commuters and press describe the jam as shifted towards HSR Layout and JP Nagar/Kanakapura Road. Cause: high-capacity elevated road discharging into a narrow signalised junction with insufficient dispersal capacity. (2) Hebbal IIT-B study: a base model that does not reproduce observed speeds was used to recommend a large capital project; the IISc reviewer concluded the recommendations were 'not scientifically supported' and that the scheme pushes congestion from one point to another. (3) IIT-B itself warns the combined scheme 'can produce a new bottleneck if both grade-separated facilities discharge large flows onto the same downstream surface link' yet concludes there is no severe spillback without showing queue results.
validation_approach: Read primary PDFs in full (IIT-B report text and figures, IISc review, RITES extract); cross-checked numbers between tables; checked OpenCity metadata through the CKAN API; Silk Board evidence from multiple press reports (Deccan Herald, OneIndia, Swarajya), since BTP has not published the underlying data.
takeaway_for_our_build: Make the demo about the downstream junction, not the flyover: (1) always include at least one signalised junction downstream of the flyover landing in the network, and report queue length and spillback onto the flyover there as headline metrics, because both Bengaluru cases fail at the landing, not on the deck. (2) Report the same metric set for every scenario (delay/vehicle, completed trips, max queue per approach, stops), with throughput-normalised delay, so comparisons cannot be cherry-picked as in the IIT-B report. (3) Ship a 'calibration check' panel that compares base-run link volumes with the RITES 2019 values using GEH and shows the observed 3.57-4.29 km/h speeds, so users see whether the base reproduces reality before trusting a scenario. (4) Expose diversion share and PCU factors as visible, editable assumptions. (5) Seed the scenario list with: base; flyover lane addition; downstream signal retiming; flyover-merge lane blockage.
